summary: ICMP timestamp rewrite by branch router causing intermittent gRPC keepalive failures and KV-cache evictions on private deploy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports elevated tail latency and periodic gRPC streaming resets on their private deployment. Behavior coincides with branch office traffic bursts.

Impact: Intermittent 5-10% of streaming requests incur 1-2s additional latency or experience a short gRPC reconnect; KV cache entries are evicted, causing regeneration of large prefix caches and increased token cost. Affects real-time scoring pipelines and causes visible degradation for end-users.

Environment: Private deployment (control plane in us-east-1), VPC peering to customer branch office via Transit Gateway; branch uses vendor-managed edge router (BR-Edge-01) with IPv4-only WAN to MPLS overlay. Redwood-serving nodes in private VPC, kernel 5.10, runtime v2.18.2.

Observed start time: 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Pattern: spikes correlated with branch office backup windows (large UDP/ICMP bursts).

Steps to reproduce: 1) From branch network generate ICMP timestamp request bursts (observed in customer's packet captures). 2) Concurrently run streaming chat sessions against pinned model rw-instruct-7b. 3) Observe intermittent TLS renegotiation and gRPC keepalive drops from serving nodes in metrics and increased cache-miss rate.

Expected: No influence of ICMP control-plane traffic on application-layer TLS/gRPC sessions.

Actual: Periodic short-lived gRPC resets and KV-cache eviction on serving nodes leading to tail latency spikes and higher token re-generation.

Notes: Customer has already validated no CPU/memory pressure on nodes and no application-level errors. Issue only reproducible when branch-originated ICMP timestamp traffic is present.
logs:
Selected excerpts from customer pcap and server logs:
- br-edge-01.pcap: repeated ICMP type 13 (timestamp request) bursts from branch subnet -> internet egress IP at 10:21:03Z.
- serving-node-12 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log: 2026-03-09T21:00:04Z grpc: keepalive timeout, closing stream id=0x1f4c. kvcache: prefix eviction policy triggered for shard s-7b-03 (cache_size dropped from 1.9GB to 128MB).
- control-plane auth logs: multiple short TLS session resumption failures from same client source IP range around same timestamps.
- tcpdump on customer NAT: see TTL and ICMP timestamp replies with altered time fields and unexpected ICMP responses during bursts.

Attached: customer_pcap_excerpt_20260309.pcap (customer-provided), runtime_tail_20260309.log
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: branch router is performing ICMP timestamp rewrite/normalization that interacts with middlebox timing heuristics in the customer's MPLS provider, triggering out-of-order packets and occasional RSTs on TLS flows. Alternative hypothesis: underlying NAT pool or conntrack entries are being stressed by the burst and causing ephemeral port reassignments that invalidate long-lived keepalive flows.

What we checked: 1) Verified serving-node kernel conntrack counts - no global exhaustion but short-lived spikes in TIME_WAIT counts aligned with incident. 2) Packet captures from serving nodes show occasional ACK reordering and duplicated ACKs. 3) TLS metrics show a pattern of short-lived session resumption failures (not full handshake failures). 4) KV-cache eviction correlates to detected stream reconnects where prefix state was not reused.

Intermediate conclusion: Evidence supports a network-induced reordering and short-lived session misbind rather than application bug. The ICMP timestamp bursts are likely symptomatic of branch backup and coincide with observed behavior.

Workaround attempted by customer: - Temporarily rate-limiting ICMP at branch egress removed the symptom. - Increasing keepalive frequency to 30s reduced impact but increased overhead.

Next steps: 1) Collect deeper synchronized pcaps from branch egress and a serving node across one reproducible window. 2) Engage customer networking team to inspect BR-Edge-01 for ICMP normalization feature or timestamp rewriting. 3) Try deploying conntrack tweaks (conntrack tcp-timeout adjustments) on customer NAT as a controlled mitigation. 4) Add additional telemetry on serving nodes to capture per-connection packet reordering counters.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:12 - Aditi Rao (Support): Logged initial report from customer. Requested pcaps and runtime logs. Customer attached pcap excerpt and runtime tail. Marked P1 due to user-impacting tail latency.

2026-03-10 16:30 - Liam Chen (SRE): Ran quick check of conntrack and TIME_WAIT on serving fleet in customer's private VPC during a controlled window; saw transient TIME_WAIT spikes but not total conntrack exhaustion. Collected tcpdump from serving-node-12 around incident window.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Customer (NimbusOps Network Ops): Confirmed BR-Edge-01 is a vendor appliance running default ICMP handling with timestamp reply normalization enabled. They will try toggling timestamp normalization in a maintenance window. They also provided a bigger pcap covering backup window.

2026-03-11 12:40 - Liam Chen (SRE): After customer disabled timestamp normalization for a 30-minute window, support metrics showed no gRPC resets and KV cache remained stable. This strongly implicates timestamp rewrite behavior. Recommended mitigation and requested a permanent configuration change on their branch router.

2026-03-12 08:20 - Aditi Rao (Support): Customer scheduled change control to disable timestamp normalization on BR-Edge-01 during their nightly maintenance. We'll monitor for recurrence and keep ticket open until one week of clean telemetry.
resolution: Mitigation path identified: disabling ICMP timestamp normalization on customer branch router removed the symptom during test window. Short-term recommended mitigations: rate-limit ICMP/time-critical control-plane bursts at branch egress and increase keepalive probing interval to 30s if needed. Long-term: customer to apply router firmware/config to stop timestamp rewrite or move backup traffic to off-peak windows; SRE to add per-connection reordering telemetry and a guard rule to flag correlated ICMP bursts that may impact streaming. Follow-up: monitor for 7 days post-change; if regressions persist, open a detailed packet-level RCA with customer's network vendor.
